data.name: Modes_Subtitle
data.value: The same TypeScript can be interpreted on the spot or compiled ahead-of-time to a .NET assembly. You choose per command.

data.name: Mode_Interpret_Desc
data.value: Tree-walking execution with instant startup and no build step — ideal for scripting, the REPL, and rapid iteration. Just point SharpTS at a file.

data.name: Mode_Compile_Desc
data.value: Emit a real .NET assembly that runs natively on the CLR. The same path can also produce a self-contained executable, a NuGet package (--pack), or a reference assembly for C# interop (--ref-asm).

data.name: Typing_Subtitle
data.value: SharpTS type-checks your whole program before it runs — then the types step aside and only the values matter.

data.name: Typing_CompileTime_Desc
data.value: The type checker validates every expression against TypeScript's rules: nominal typing for classes, structural typing for interfaces. A type error stops the program before it runs.

data.name: Typing_Runtime_Desc
data.value: Once the checks pass, the types drop away and your program runs on plain values — just like compiled JavaScript. The safety you get while writing costs nothing while running.

data.name: Typing_Caption
data.value: Structural typing in action: Dog satisfies Walkable simply because it has a walk() method — no explicit "implements" required.

data.name: Dotnet_Subtitle
data.value: Because SharpTS targets the CLR, your TypeScript becomes a first-class .NET citizen — calling into .NET and callable from it.

data.name: Cap1_Body
data.value: Reach into the BCL with the @DotNetType decorator — StringBuilder, Guid, DateTime, TimeSpan — with automatic conversion and overload resolution.

data.name: Cap2_Body
data.value: Compile with --ref-asm to get a reference assembly, then instantiate your TypeScript classes and call their methods directly from C#, fully typed.

data.name: Cap3_Body
data.value: Produce a .NET assembly, a self-contained executable, or a versioned NuGet package straight from your TypeScript source.

data.name: Cap4_Body
data.value: Add SharpTS.Sdk to a project file and build .ts files as part of your normal .NET build, driven by tsconfig.json.

data.name: Cap5_Body
data.value: A language server (the vscode-sharpts extension) plus .d.ts declaration generation give you completion and type info in your editor.

data.name: Cap6_Body
data.value: Classes, generics, async/await, generators, decorators, modules, Map and Set, BigInt, Date, RegExp, Symbol, and JSON.

data.name: Cta_Body
data.value: The best way to understand the pipeline is to run code through it.
